key_insight: CAMBY will investigate how brain network structure and function relate to persistent attention and mental health symptoms after adolescent concussion—not AI cancer drug discovery.
clinical_relevance: Identifying disrupted brain networks could inform future targeted neurostimulation trials for persistent symptoms after concussion.
method: Prospective observational study of adolescents aged 12–18 with a concussion history.
Compare participants with persistent symptoms against recovered concussion controls.
Integrate structural MRI, functional MEG, and neuropsychological assessments collected at least one month after concussion.
evidence_signal: This protocol plans group comparisons and mediation analyses linking brain network features to neuropsychological outcomes; no study results are reported.
watch_item: The observational design cannot establish causality or demonstrate that neurostimulation improves symptoms.
paper_title: Concussion, Attention, and Mental Health: A Brain Network Study in Youth (CAMBY) - Study Protocol
